message_analysis: Crystal clear single message: ChatGPT users are underutilizing the tool by asking plain questions; the R.C.F. method (Role, Constraint, Format) unlocks elite outputs. Every scene reinforces this without filler. Hook promises a trick, Scene 3 delivers it, Scene 4 proves it, Scene 5 scales it. The angle is fresh — framing ChatGPT prompting as 'method acting' is original and memorable. Shame-hook + immediate fix is proven TikTok structure. Viewers will share because it resolves a real pain point (mediocre ChatGPT outputs) with a memorable, actionable framework.
scroll_stop_analysis: First 1.5 seconds nail the curiosity-shame loop: '10%' accusation + visual impact (shattering text, camera shake) creates immediate tension. Scene 2 doubles down with rapid red-X stamps—pattern interrupts maintain momentum. Scene 4's split-screen comparison is a powerful retention driver (plain vs. elite side-by-side). Pacing is tight at 37s with no dead air. Emotion arc builds naturally: shock → curiosity → revelation → intrigue → urgency → satisfying loop-back. Feels native to TikTok (kinetic text, rapid cuts, visual metaphors) not like a lecture. The 10%→100% bookend is psychologically satisfying. Would absolutely stop scrolls.
